modules.name: ShortenService
modules.responsibility: Accept a long URL, validate it, generate or accept a custom short code, persist the mapping, and return the short URL. Owns code-generation strategy and collision handling.
injection_points: CodeGenerator (base62 counter vs random vs custom)

modules.name: RedirectService
modules.responsibility: Resolve a short code to its target URL and issue an HTTP redirect. Emits a click event asynchronously without blocking the redirect path.

modules.name: StatsService
modules.responsibility: Record click events and aggregate per-link click statistics (totals, by-day, by-referrer). Reads are eventually consistent with the redirect hot path.

modules.name: RateLimiter
modules.responsibility: Enforce per-client request quotas on write-heavy endpoints (shorten) and optionally on redirects. Returns allow/deny plus retry metadata.
injection_points: key extraction policy (IP vs API key)

modules.name: ApiGateway
modules.responsibility: HTTP boundary: route requests, parse/validate input, apply rate limiting, map domain results and errors to HTTP responses. Holds no business logic.
interfaces:
class Handler(Protocol):
    def handle(self, request: HttpRequest) -> HttpResponse: ...
injection_points: All service dependencies wired via composition root

modules.name: Persistence
modules.responsibility: Provide repository implementations for links and click events behind storage-agnostic Protocols. Default to SQLite; swappable to Postgres/Redis.
interfaces:
class LinkRepository(Protocol):
    def save(self, link: ShortLink) -> None: ...
    def get_by_code(self, code: str) -> ShortLink | None: ...
    def get_by_url(self, url: str) -> ShortLink | None: ...
    def delete(self, code: str) -> None: ...

class ClickRepository(Protocol):
    def append(self, event: ClickEvent) -> None: ...
    def aggregate(self, code: str) -> ClickStats: ...

fields.name: created_by
fields.notes: API key id or hashed client identifier; nullable for anonymous

fields.name: ip_trunc
fields.notes: truncated/anonymized IP (last octet zeroed) or salted hash; PII-minimized

fields.name: key
fields.notes: client identity: API key or hashed IP

ux_flows.name: Shorten a URL
steps: Gateway extracts client key and calls RateLimiter.check
URLValidator checks scheme/host; ShortenService generates or accepts code
ux_flows.success_criteria: Valid URL returns a working short link in a single request; p95 < 100ms
i18n_considerations: Error messages localizable via message keys

ux_flows.name: Follow a short link (redirect)
steps: If active and not expired, enqueue ClickEvent and return 301/302 Location
ux_flows.success_criteria: Redirect issued in p95 < 30ms; click recording never blocks redirect
i18n_considerations: Locale-neutral redirect; no localized body needed

ux_flows.name: View click stats
ux_flows.success_criteria: Owner retrieves totals + by-day breakdown in one request
error_states: 403 if ownership enforced and caller is not owner
i18n_considerations: Dates returned as ISO-8601 UTC; client formats per locale

customer_journey: A developer integrating link-shortening discovers the API, sends a long URL to POST /api/shorten, and immediately receives a compact short URL. They share it; end users click the short link and are redirected transparently to the destination with negligible latency. The developer later queries /api/stats/{code} to see how many clicks the link received, when, and from where (referrers), without exposing raw visitor identities. Throughout, abusive or runaway clients are throttled by rate limiting so the service stays responsive for everyone. The experience feels instant, predictable, and privacy-respecting.

experience_metric.name: time_to_first_short_link
experience_metric.target: Shorten a URL in <=1 API call and receive a working redirect in <=2 total requests
experience_metric.measurement: Count requests from shorten to successful redirect; redirect p95 latency < 30ms

architecture_decisions.title: Decouple click recording from the redirect hot path
architecture_decisions.context: Every redirect must be fast and reliable, but we also want click analytics. Writing analytics synchronously on the redirect path couples availability and latency of redirects to the stats subsystem and its storage.
architecture_decisions.decision: RedirectService depends on a ClickRecorder Protocol and emits click events through it without awaiting durable aggregation. The default implementation enqueues events (in-process queue, swappable to a durable queue) consumed by StatsService. Redirect succeeds even if recording fails.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Separation of concerns and the Dependency Inversion Principle: redirects depend on an abstraction, not a concrete analytics store. This keeps redirect latency low and isolates failures, while remaining testable via a fake recorder.
consequences: Click stats are eventually consistent, not real-time exact
Need a background consumer and backpressure/drop policy for the queue
Possible loss of a small number of click events under crash before flush
Redirect path stays fast and independently deployable/scalable

architecture_decisions.title: Use a pluggable base62 code generator with collision retry
architecture_decisions.context: Short codes must be compact, URL-safe, and unique. Options include sequential base62 of an auto-increment id, random codes, or hash-based codes.
architecture_decisions.decision: Define a CodeGenerator Protocol with a default random base62 generator (length 7) and a repository uniqueness check with bounded retry on collision; custom aliases bypass generation but are validated for uniqueness.
architecture_decisions.rationale: Open/Closed Principle: strategy is swappable without touching ShortenService. Random base62 avoids leaking sequential volume and enumeration of links.
consequences: Small collision-retry cost at high volume
Code space (62^7) is ample for foreseeable scale
Sequential strategy can be injected later if ordered codes are desired

threat_model.description: Abusive clients flood POST /api/shorten or hammer redirects, exhausting storage and capacity.
threat_model.mitigation: Per-client token-bucket RateLimiter on write and read endpoints with Retry-After; configurable quotas keyed by API key or hashed IP.

threat_model.description: Open redirect abuse: attacker shortens links to malicious/internal targets (phishing, SSRF-style internal hosts) to leverage the service's trust.
threat_model.mitigation: URLValidator enforces http/https only, blocks private/loopback/link-local hosts and credentials-in-URL; optional domain allow/deny list; safe-browsing check as future hook.

threat_model.description: Click logs containing visitor IPs and user agents could deanonymize end users or leak browsing behavior if exposed or over-retained.
threat_model.mitigation: Store IP truncated/hashed with salt, coarse user-agent, time-bounded retention (90 days) with automatic purge; stats endpoint returns aggregates only, never raw events; ownership check on stats read.

privacy_inventory.purpose: Abuse detection and coarse geo/click analytics
privacy_inventory.retention: Stored truncated/hashed; raw IP never persisted; aggregates kept indefinitely, event rows purged after 90 days
privacy_inventory.encryption: At rest via DB encryption; IP one-way salted hash or last-octet truncation in application layer
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Purge ClickEvents by code or by client identity; scheduled retention job deletes events older than 90 days

privacy_inventory.retention: Reduced to browser/OS family at write time; full string not retained
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Deleted with associated ClickEvent rows on purge or per-code deletion

privacy_inventory.retention: Lifetime of the link; stored as id/hash not raw secret
privacy_inventory.encryption: Secret material hashed; at rest encryption
privacy_inventory.erasure_path: Account deletion cascades to nullify created_by and remove owned links on request

i18n_plan.framework: gettext-style message catalogs with message keys; no hardcoded user-facing strings in services
i18n_plan.rtl_strategy: API is RTL-neutral (JSON/data only); any future web UI uses logical CSS properties and dir=auto. Hostnames normalized to punycode; timestamps emitted as ISO-8601 UTC for client-side localization.
i18n_plan.number_date_format: Server emits ISO-8601/raw integers; localization deferred to client

open_questions: Is authentication/ownership required for shorten and stats, or is the service fully anonymous (affects created_by, stats access control, and erasure)?
What is the expected scale (links/day, redirects/sec)? Determines whether SQLite suffices or Redis/Postgres + durable queue are needed from iteration 1.
Do links expire by default, and is custom expiry/TTL a required feature?
Are custom aliases a supported feature in iteration 1, or codes only?
What is the authoritative rate-limit policy (limits, window, key = IP vs API key) and is it per-endpoint?
Is exact real-time click counting required, or is eventual consistency (per ADR-001) acceptable to the customer?

sections.title: Module Boundaries
sections.content: Six modules: ShortenService, RedirectService, StatsService, RateLimiter, ApiGateway, Persistence. All cross-module dependencies are Protocol interfaces wired at a composition root, enabling DI and test fakes. Redirect hot path is isolated from analytics.

sections.title: Data Model
sections.content: ShortLink (code PK, long_url, created_at, created_by?, expires_at?, is_active), ClickEvent (id PK, code FK, ts, ip_trunc?, referrer?, user_agent?), derived ClickStats, RateBucket. PII concentrated in ClickEvent and created_by; minimized via truncation/hashing.

sections.title: Key Flows
sections.content: Shorten (POST /api/shorten), Redirect (GET /{code}), View stats (GET /api/stats/{code}). Redirect prioritizes latency; shorten and stats are rate-limited; all error states mapped to HTTP codes (400/404/409/410/429/500).

sections.title: Architecture Decisions
sections.content: ADR-001 decouples click recording from redirect via a ClickRecorder Protocol (eventual consistency for low-latency redirects). ADR-002 uses a pluggable base62 CodeGenerator with collision retry and validated custom aliases.

sections.title: Security & Privacy
sections.content: Top threats: DoS (token-bucket rate limiting), open-redirect/SSRF (URL validation + host blocklist), visitor deanonymization (IP truncation/hashing, 90-day retention, aggregates-only stats). PII: visitor IP, user agent, referrer, creator id — all with documented retention and erasure paths.

sections.title: Open Questions
sections.content: Auth/ownership model, expected scale and storage backend, default link expiry, custom alias support, authoritative rate-limit policy, and whether real-time exact click counts are required all remain open and may revise module and data-model decisions.
